history.content: IBM Watson® Speech to Text service

The IBM Watson® Speech to Text service provides an API that uses IBM's speech-recognition capabilities to produce transcripts of spoken audio. It can transcribe speech from various languages and audio formats, and it can return detailed information about many aspects of the audio. The service supports two sampling rates, broadband and narrowband, and it returns all JSON response content in the UTF-8 character set. The Watson packages for this service are deprecated, and you should use the Watson SDKs for related functionality. For more information, you can refer to the Speech to Text API reference and documentation.
How many languages does it support?

The IBM Watson® Speech to Text service supports speech recognition for many languages. The service offers different models for the languages it supports, with most language models available for general production use, while a few are still in beta. 
The supported languages include:
Arabic (Modern Standard)
 Chinese (Mandarin)
 Czech
Dutch (Belgian and Netherlands)
 English (Australian, Indian, United Kingdom, and United States)
French (Canadian and France)
German
Hindi (Indian)
Italian
Japanese
Korean
Portuguese (Brazilian)
Spanish (Castilian and Latin American)
Swedish
How do I generate credentials for my instance?

Log in to your IBM Cloud account.
Go to Resource list > Services and Software > Databases.
Click on your Netezza Performance Server instance. You are now on the Service instance details page where you can find information about endpoints for accessing the web console, the API server, and the database.
Go to the Service Credentials tab.
Click New Credentials.
Type a name to assing to your credentials.
Select the IAM role that was assigned to you to manage the instance.
Click Add.
If your credentials were generated successfully, you can expand the newly created credential entry to view them.

In most cases, rotating credentials is a straight-forward process:
Generate a replacement service credential. For more information, see How can I generate service credentials?.
Replace the current credential with the newly generated credential.
Delete the no-longer-used service credential.
However, when you rotate the credentials for a replication, if you are using legacy credentials in the replication document, the replication starts from the beginning. To ensure that changes arrive in a timely manner, we advise you to create a new replication once it catches up with deleting the previous replication and the associated service credential.
